TREPP US CMBS — MONTHLY DELINQUENCY, YEAR-APART COMPARISON

column6: Delinquent balance divided by covered outstanding balance.
Office segment of the same covered universe.
Non-agency CMBS multifamily; not all US apartments.
Retail segment; not a mall-only peer set.

column2: US conduit, SASB and certain large-loan floating-rate CMBS. CRE CLOs, agency/GSE securities, cell towers and other nontraditional collateral excluded.
30+ days delinquent, nonperforming matured loans, foreclosure and REO. Performing matured balloon loans are excluded from the headline measure.

Covered outstanding balance includes defeased loans. August 2025 published totals: $44.1B delinquent / $604.6B outstanding, both rounded. August 2026 balance totals were not supplied in the reviewed public release.
Rates are published provider outputs; rounded balance totals may not reproduce the rate exactly. Population can change through issuance, amortization and resolutions; this is not a fixed cohort.

column1: KBRA CRE CLO — CUMULATIVE HISTORICAL STUDY THROUGH MARCH 2026

column6: Ever 60+ days delinquent in the observed study.
Additional to payment defaults; not current delinquencies.
Incremental loans beyond the default categories.
Combined cumulative distress measure; not loss severity.

column2: 6,919 loans across 227 CLOs issued July 2013–March 2025, followed through March 2026. Count weighted, historical cumulative observations; seasoning varies.
KBRA reports 86.5% of defaulted loans resolved through repayment or repurchase. Exit from the CLO does not establish the property’s final loss or creditor recovery.
Use Trepp office/retail/multifamily context for comparable CMBS loans. Use KBRA only as historical context for CLO loans after checking vintage and study eligibility.
Bank construction credits (including OZK) and agency Park Greene have no matched benchmark established here. Do not apply these CMBS/CLO rates to those populations.
101 event/lead rows are selected cases, may repeat collateral and span multiple years. No market loss, delinquency or default rate is calculated from them.
For bank construction and agency loans, obtain a same-period provider series with a documented numerator, exposure population and weighting. No substitute rate has been invented.
